title: Sample Runbook
subject: A structurally complete example — every field the scaffold renders
summary: This is not a real runbook. It exists so the scaffold can be rendered and checked without inventing content, and so a new runbook can be written by replacing the values rather than guessing the shape. Every field described in references/runbook-spec.md appears at least once below.

leads.title: Two things to know before step one
body: This is sample content. The prose fields accept inline HTML — emphasis, inline code, and links to phases all work. Titles and labels are escaped instead, so write those as plain text.

Ids are the progress keys. Renaming a step id orphans whatever the reader had already ticked, which is why new steps get appended or given a suffixed id like p1.2b rather than renumbering the ones after them.
items: Phases run top to bottom; steps inside a phase are sequential by construction.
Cross-phase ordering is declared per step with dependsOn.

claudeBudget.title: Working through this with Claude
claudeBudget.note: Order-of-magnitude figures for the phases marked for tandem work. They measure the conversation, not the setup — a single stubborn failure can cost more than several clean phases.

phases.title: Pre-flight
phases.intent: Confirm the machine can actually do the work before installing anything on it. Every hour lost to a long build is lost here, discovering a missing prerequisite at hour nine.

steps.title: Check the toolchain versions
steps.do: Run the version check below. If any tool is missing, install it before going further.
steps.why: Later phases assume a modern Node and a working git. Finding out otherwise in phase 02 means unwinding a partial install.

verify.expect: v20.x or newer. If Node is missing entirely: sudo apt install -y nodejs.

steps.title: Read how the disk is laid out
steps.do: Nothing to execute. This step exists so the paths used later in the runbook are not a surprise.
notes: Anything under /tmp is assumed disposable between phases.

steps.title: Decide whether to keep the existing database
steps.do: Decide now: migrate the existing data, or start clean. Write the answer down — phase 02 branches on it.
steps.why: Both routes are reasonable, but switching between them after phase 02 means redoing the schema work.

callouts.title: Hard to undo
body: Starting clean drops the existing rows. Take a dump first even if you are confident: pg_dump app > ~/app-backup.sql.

verification.title: You are ready to start when both of these are true.
verification.expect: A version string followed by paths ok, and a written answer to the database question.

phases.title: Provision the host
phases.intent: Get a reachable machine with the right ports open, so the deploy in phase 02 has somewhere to land.

steps.title: Create the server instance
steps.do: Create a small instance in the region closest to your users, and record its IP address.
steps.why: The smallest tier is enough for the build; resizing later is a reboot, not a rebuild, so start cheap.

callouts.title: Region matters more than size
body: Latency to your users is set at creation time and cannot be changed without rebuilding. Instance size can be changed in a minute.

verify.expect: One reply. If it times out, ICMP may simply be blocked — try SSH instead before assuming the host is down.

steps.title: Open only the ports you need
steps.do: Allow 22, 80 and 443. Deny everything else inbound.
steps.why: A default-open host gets found by scanners within hours. This is cheap now and expensive to retrofit after a compromise.

commands.caption: run as root
commands.code:
ufw default deny incoming
ufw default allow outgoing
ufw allow 22/tcp
ufw allow 80,443/tcp
ufw --force enable

verify.expect: Status active, default deny (incoming), and exactly three allow rules.

steps.title: Point the domain at the server
steps.do: Blocked until the instance above exists and has an IP. Once it does, add an A record for the apex domain.
steps.why: DNS propagation is the slowest thing in this runbook, so it is started early even though nothing depends on it until the final phase.

steps.title: SSH key was already added during signup
steps.do: Nothing to do — this was completed when the account was created. It is listed so the picture is complete.

verification.title: The host is ready when you can reach it and nothing else can.
verification.expect: A login with no password prompt, printing Status: active.

phases.title: Deploy and verify
phases.intent: Put the application on the host and prove it serves traffic, so the runbook ends on evidence rather than assumption.

steps.title: Build and copy the release
steps.do: Build locally, then copy the output to /srv/app on the server.
steps.why: Building on the small instance is slower than building locally and copying the result, and it keeps build tooling off the production host.
notes: --delete removes files on the server that are no longer in the build. That is intentional — stale assets are a common source of confusing cache behaviour.

steps.title: Confirm the site answers over HTTPS
steps.do: Request the homepage over HTTPS and confirm a 200 with a valid certificate.

verify.expect: 200 0. A non-zero second number means the certificate did not verify — usually DNS has not fully propagated yet.

verification.title: The deploy is real when a fresh browser can load it.
verification.expect: 200, and the page loads in a private window with no certificate warning.

completion.title: The whole runbook is done when this one command tells you so.
completion.code: node -v && ufw status | head -1 && curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<your-domain>/
completion.expect: A Node version, Status: active, and 200 — in that order, with no errors between them.

gotchas.symptom: curl returns 000 and hangs for a while first
gotchas.cause: The firewall is enabled but the port rule was never added, so packets are dropped rather than refused
gotchas.fix: Check ufw status verbose. A dropped connection times out; a refused one fails immediately — the delay itself tells you which.

gotchas.symptom: The certificate is invalid in the browser but curl is happy
gotchas.cause: The certificate covers the apex domain but the browser was pointed at the www subdomain
gotchas.fix: Issue the certificate for both names, or redirect one to the other at the web server.

gotchas.symptom: Old assets keep being served after a deploy
gotchas.cause: rsync was run without --delete, leaving previous build output in place
gotchas.fix: Re-run the copy with --delete, then hard-reload. Content-hashed filenames make this mostly invisible until it is not.

outOfScope.title: Deliberately not in this runbook
body: These are all reasonable next steps, and none of them are needed to reach the completion check above. They are listed so their absence reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
items: Monitoring and alerting — worth doing, but it needs a running service to watch first.
A second environment for staging — the same steps, run twice, with different names.
Automated deploys from CI — start by deploying by hand until the steps are boring.
